Order money leaves out lowball orders priced under a quarter of the market.

Reading the economy

Money on the baltop is the total held by every player on the money leaderboard, the best single measure of how much money exists on the server. Concentration shows how much of it sits with the very richest players, and the distribution groups everyone by balance so you can see where a typical player sits.

Money in buy orders is demand that is waiting to be filled, and what orders paid out in the last day shows how much of it actually turned into trades. In the charts, watch the trend rather than single readings: a lasting step up or down usually comes from a real event on the server, such as a wave of bans.

How to read these prices

Every item has two sides. The asking price is what sellers on the auction house want for one item, based on the cheapest listings so a single odd listing cannot skew it. The top buy order is what a buyer has already offered to pay, so it is the price you get if you sell right now.

The gap between the two is the spread. A small spread means buyers and sellers agree on what an item is worth; a large one can mean an opportunity to flip, or simply an item that rarely trades. Items with only a handful of listings deserve a second look before you trust their price, and enchanted gear is priced separately for each combination of enchantments.
